evals.prompt: New people keep tripping over the getting-started steps in the README for our orders API. Can you write a setup script so they can just run one thing? The repo is in evals/files/node-postgres-app.
evals.expected_output: An executable setup.sh at the repo root that checks Node against .nvmrc, installs with pnpm (not npm/yarn), copies .env.example to .env without overwriting, starts the db via `docker compose up -d db` (not a hand-rolled docker run) with a --no-docker skip flag, runs prisma migrate/seed only when the db phase ran, and prints next steps (pnpm dev, localhost:4000). Script verified with bash -n, --help, a real run, and a re-run; test artifacts cleaned up.
expectations: A setup script exists in the repo and is executable
Script passes `bash -n` syntax check
`--help` prints help and exits 0 without running any setup or leaking comment separators
Script never overwrites an existing .env (guarded copy)
Test-run artifacts (.env, .venv, node_modules, bin/, ...) were cleaned up afterwards
Final report says the script was actually run a second time to check idempotency
Script checks the Docker daemon is reachable, not just that the `docker` binary exists
Installs with pnpm (matching pnpm-lock.yaml), not npm/yarn
Checks the Node version against .nvmrc
Starts Postgres via the repo's docker compose file rather than a hand-rolled `docker run`
Offers a skip flag for the database/docker phase
Runs Prisma migrations (db:migrate / prisma migrate)
Next steps mention `pnpm dev` and port 4000
